A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a novel cost function to semi-supervised learning that encourages compact clustering in the latent space to enable better class separation.

we propose a novel semi-supervised learning approach that combines the benefits of label propagation with efficient, inductively inferred regularization, does not require modification to a network architecture and can be easily applied to any neural network.

we propose a novel cost function that regularizes the network to form clusters in the latent space, while encouraging the network to form a single cluster per class, and that we evaluate our cost function against the state-of-the-art on three benchmarks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the latent space of a neural network can be effectively regularized to facilitate separation of classes.
a simple, graph-based cost function is a powerful tool for semi-supervised deep learning.
